transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Park (Redwood SE), Anya Feldman (Redwood Product), Ravi Menon (Lumina Head of AI), Aisha Gomez (Lumina ML Eng), Toni Brown (Lumina Privacy), Marco Li (Lumina PM)

Auto-generated Summary (note: brief):
Samir opened with a high-level demo of Redwood's Eval and Optimize surfaces — prompt set management, regression alerting, and A/B comparison flows. Customer focused on quality monitoring for production chat agents used in triage workflows and regulatory needs (HIPAA, SOC2). POC scope discussed: ingest prompt sets, establish golden labels, run A/B comparisons across quantized model variants, and set up regression alerts tied to specific prompt cohorts. Next steps: pricing, security docs, POC kickoff scheduling.

Topics: prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons, Optimize recommendations, Dedicated vs Hosted, SOC2/HIPAA, POC scope

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samir from Redwood, AE for Lumina. Today Jules will walk through the evaluation/monitoring demo — prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B compares. We got about 45 minutes right?
[00:12] Ravi: Yep that works, thanks. Toni's on for security parts and Aisha will cover data folks questions.
[00:18] Jules: Cool. Quick agenda: show Console workflows for prompt sets, create an eval, demo regression alert config, then show A/B compare and how Optimize suggests batching/quant configs. We'll try to keep it hands-on.
[00:30] Aisha: Quick ask — we care about labeled golden responses per triage category. Can we ingest CSVs or do you prefer JSONL?
[00:38] Jules: Both. Console takes CSV/JSONL for prompt sets; the eval harness normalizes them. Slight note: if you have complex multi-turn, JSONL with context fields is cleaner.
[00:49] Marco: We have a lot of partially redacted PHI in examples, how do we handle that in the sandbox?
[00:56] Anya: Good question. For the hosted demo we recommend synthetic or scrubbed data; for the POC you can run private deployment or Dedicated and we can enable encryption at-rest keys and tighter logging. Toni, we can flag the SOC2/HIPAA items after.
[01:10] Toni: Yes, we need to see KMS integration details and the audit log retention options. Also, are transcripts stored in plain text in hosted?
[01:18] Samir: By default hosted stores logs for X days, can be configured; dedicated/private gives you control. We'll share the security whitepaper.

[02:05] Jules: Ok jumping into the Console — starting at the Eval tab. Forgive the screen lag — this is a demo env. On the left you see Prompt Sets. I'm going to upload a sample CSV (we'll pretend this is Lumina triage prompts).
[02:20] [typing sounds]
[02:26] Jules: Upload done. You can tag prompts into cohorts — e.g., 'cardio-triage', 'mental-health', 'billing-queries'. This lets you create cohort-specific metrics and alerts.
[02:40] Aisha: Nice, cohorts are what we wanted. Can we attach golden labels per prompt row?
[02:45] Jules: Yup — there's a 'expected_answer' column mapping. The eval harness will compute exact-match, token-F1, and a customizable similarity metric.
[02:56] Ravi: That similarity metric — is that semantic embedding based? I ask because we need tolerance for synonyms.
[03:02] Jules: It uses an embedding-backed scorer by default (we call it the semantic comparator) but you can plug in custom metric functions via the Eval API.

[04:10] [screen change] Jules: Now I'll run an initial eval across three model variants: open-llama-7b-quant, redwood-7b-static (example), and a higher-accuracy hosted variant. This will produce per-prompt scores and a baseline.
[04:25] [pause]
[04:30] Jules: Results back — here's the table. You can sort by cohort, by metric. Notice the 'regression risk' column which is a composite that flags prompts with sudden score drops relative to baseline.
[04:45] Marco: Is the baseline version pinned? We want to be able to pin a golden baseline to compare future releases.
[04:51] Jules: Totally. You pin baseline by model/version + prompt set snapshot. For rollouts we support A/B traffic routing at the routing layer so you can do canary and compare.

[05:30] Aisha: Walk me through the regression alerts — we want proactive alerts only for clinically sensitive cohorts.
[05:38] Jules: Sure. In Alerts, create a new rule, scope to cohort 'cardio-triage', choose metric 'token-f1' and threshold delta -8% relative to pinned baseline, set rolling window 24h and minimum sample size 50. Then choose notification: email, webhook, or PagerDuty.
[05:58] Ravi: Can we tie the webhook to our internal ticketing so an alert auto-opens an incident?
[06:03] Jules: Yep — webhook payload includes prompt id, model versions, metric diffs, and sample inputs. (Small caveat: we scrub PHI if scrub option enabled — otherwise we deliver raw inputs if you allow it.)

[07:10] Toni: About scrubbing — what is your recommended approach for PII/PHI? We need to be able to prove to auditors what was retained or redacted.
[07:18] Anya: We have an integrated redaction pipeline — you can enable regex-based scrubbing, or for advanced customers we run a client-side sanitization hook in the private deployment so sensitive tokens never reach Redwood. We'll share the tech note.
[07:32] Toni: Good. Also retention windows and the ability to delete prompt sets on request matter to us.
[07:38] Samir: Those are supported, Toni — we'll include the details in the SOC2/HIPAA scoping doc.

[08:50] Jules: Back to A/B comparisons — I'll create an A/B experiment between two model configs: one is quantized with lower cost, the other is a float16 higher-accuracy variant. We'll route 20% traffic to variant B. The Console then runs the eval on live traffic 'shadow' mode and accumulates metrics per cohort.
[09:10] Marco: Does live traffic evaling add latency? We can't add p99 latency to the user path.
[09:16] Jules: We do it in shadow mode — the eval calls are asynchronous and we don't block user responses. For synchronous eval (if you want exact end-to-end scoring), we recommend sampling at low qps or running batched offline evals.
[09:30] Ravi: What's the data pipeline for that? Are you storing full user inputs?
[09:34] Jules: You can choose to send full transcripts or hashed inputs. For compliance you can limit to metadata + embedding only.

[10:45] Aisha: On the Optimize suggestions — does Redwood automatically recommend quantization or batching settings per workload?
[10:52] Jules: Yes, Optimize analyzes token distributions, latency SLOs, and cost targets. It will propose quantization level, KV cache sizes, and batching configs. In the Console we show expected token-cost delta and estimated p95 latency impact.
[11:05] Aisha: Show us an example?
[11:07] Jules: Sure. Here Optimize suggests switching to int8 quant for the 'billing' cohort and bumping batch size to 8; estimated cost down 42% and p95 up 15ms — well within our 300ms SLO.
[11:22] Ravi: That p95 increase is acceptable. But for triage we can't risk hallucinations — how do you validate that quantization doesn't harm QA?
[11:30] Jules: That's why Eval + A/B are linked: you can run the same prompt sets through quantized model in the eval harness and compare semantic similarity, token-F1, and if needed human label a sample to confirm. Optimize won't auto-apply changes to prod without a rollout/approval step.

[12:40] [01:12:40? — note human timestamps keep minutes; we'll keep consistency]
[12:42] Marco: For the POC we want to test two things: batch cost wins and regression detection sensitivity. Proposed POC: ingest 5k prompts, run baseline eval, run A/B live shadow for 2 weeks, and set up alerting. Feels long — can you compress?
[12:58] Jules: You can compress by running synthetic replay at high QPS in a Dedicated environment. That gives you faster stat significance. We recommend 1–2 weeks of real traffic ideally, but synthetic replay can get you quick insight.

[14:05] Aisha: For the synthetic replay, do we need to provide session context? Our prompts are multi-turn.
[14:12] Jules: Provide the context field in JSONL; console supports context windows. For KV caching behavior we simulate via sequence length distribution in replay.

[15:00] Ravi: Security again — if we go Dedicated, where is the control plane? Is it still Redwood-managed?
[15:05] Samir: For Dedicated you get control plane separation for logs and capacity, but the control plane can be hosted in a customer VPC or in Redwood-managed with strict tenancy. For fully private on-prem, you get the private control plane option. We'll map this in the security doc.
[15:20] Toni: Important for us: key management integration (HSM/KMS) and SSO integration with Okta.
[15:26] Anya: Supported — SAML/Okta for SSO and KMS via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSM for on-prem.

[16:40] Jules: Jumping back to the Console, I'm going to show a regression alert firing example. I trigger a model shift in the demo by changing the quant parameter — you'll see prompts in 'mental-health' cohort drop and an alert get created.
[16:55] [demo triggers]
[17:02] Jules: Alert created. It shows affected prompt IDs, sample inputs (redacted option on), delta percentages, and suggested rollback action — we also have an auto-fallback policy that can revert traffic to baseline model if severity crosses threshold.
[17:18] Ravi: Can that auto-fallback be limited to certain routes? We only want auto-fallback for critical triage flows.
[17:25] Jules: Yes, you scope fallback policies per route or per cohort.

[18:40] Marco: On A/B analysis, what are the statistical tests you run? We need confidence intervals and p-values for differences.
[18:47] Jules: We provide bootstrap confidence intervals and a two-sample permutation test for the chosen metric. The UI surfaces significance and also suggests minimum samples needed for X% power.
[18:59] Aisha: Great — we need that for compliance reporting.

[20:10] Toni: A quick procurement question — can we get a contract addendum for HIPAA?
[20:16] Samir: Yes, we have a HIPAA BA template and enterprise klause addendum. Toni, I'll attach the legal contact and the template.

[22:00] Jules: One more feature: you can couple Eval runs to CI. When you update prompt sets or model version in your infra, you can trigger automated evals so regressions are detected before deploy.
[22:12] Ravi: That's huge. We want that in our CI pipeline. Which CI systems integrate easily?
[22:18] Jules: Any system that can call a REST API — we have example GitHub Actions and Jenkins scripts; will share snippets.

[24:00] Aisha: For the POC data exports — can we export all eval artifacts including diffs and annotated examples for auditors?
[24:10] Jules: Yes — export to JSONL or CSV, and you can push to your S3/GCS bucket. For private deployment, we can write directly to your bucket with VPC access.

[25:22] Marco: Competitors question — Ravi: have you evaluated OpenAI or Anthropic for monitoring?
[25:30] Ravi: They're okay but lack a unified eval/optimize product that ties to routing and private deployments.
[25:35] Samir: That's been a common gap we hear — Redwood aims to unify runtime + eval + optimize.

[26:40] Jules: Back to the A/B UI — here's a waterfall diff by cohort. For 'billing' cohort, quantized model lost 2% semantic similarity but saved 60% cost; for 'cardio' cohort it dropped 9% which triggers a red flag.
[26:58] Toni: So we'd set a policy to block quantized rollout on 'cardio' cohort unless human-reviewed.
[27:05] Jules: Exactly. You can make approval gates per cohort.

[28:30] Ravi: Operationally, who at Redwood will run the initial POC? We want an engineer with deep latency and quantization experience.
[28:38] Samir: We'll assign Jules as SE lead and Anya product as POC coordinator. Samir will be AE owner. I'll put names in the next steps.

[30:15] Aisha: A small nit: your Console sometimes labels 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' in the transcribed logs — just kidding, but we've seen weird labels in some exported artifacts in other vendors.
[30:28] Jules: Ha, the transcript generator can be messy. We try to keep internal names consistent though.

[31:50] Marco: Pricing question: is Optimize included or is it an add-on?
[31:55] Samir: Optimize is a paid add-on. For pilots we can include it in the POC credit package. We'll detail pricing tiers in the follow-up.

[33:10] Aisha: For our evaluation metrics, the legal folks want to tie model changes to downstream user outcomes — can Redwood correlate prompt-level regressions to macro KPIs?
[33:22] Jules: We can ingest your downstream KPI logs and map user sessions to prompt cohorts; then run correlation analysis to see if metric deltas predict KPI delta. That is part of a deeper engagement but doable.

[34:45] Toni: Regarding SSO, can we provision RBAC roles for auditors who should see eval reports but not keys?
[34:52] Anya: Yes — Console has role-based permissions and you can scope read-only auditor roles to Eval and Audit logs. Keys and KMS admin is separate.

[36:00] Samir: Quick recaps before we finish: POC scope suggestion — ingest 5k prompt rows across 3 cohorts, run baseline eval, run A/B shadow for 2 weeks OR synthetic replay, set up 3 cohort-specific regression alerts, and demo auto-fallback for critical cohort. Pricing/contract + security docs to follow.
[36:18] Ravi: That sounds right. Can we compress timeline to start POC next week?
[36:25] Samir: We can aim for a Mar 16 engineering kickoff. Samir will send available times.

[37:45] Jules: I'll also include a small notebook demonstrating how to call the Eval API programmatically, plus a sample GitHub Action to trigger evals.
[37:55] Aisha: Please include the sample for multi-turn prompt JSONL.

[39:10] Toni: One last compliance check: will the POC logs be preserved beyond the pilot? We may want them for audit post-mortem but also need right-to-be-forgotten.
[39:20] Samir: Retention is configurable and we support deletion. Toni, we'll include retention options in the scoping doc.

[41:00] Marco: Any blockers on our side to start? Aisha: we'll anonymize the data set and deliver prompt sets and labels.
[41:08] Aisha: Yes, we'll prepare a scrubbed CSV and a second JSONL with context. Expect those by 2026-03-10.

[42:30] Jules: Ok final demo note: if you plan to run human-in-the-loop audits, Console lets you export a sampling queue for manual review and you can write back labels to the prompt set.
[42:45] Ravi: Good. That will help us for clinical QA flow.

[44:00] Samir: Alright, thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the pricing, security pack, and proposed times for Mar 16 kickoff. Jules will share the notebook + eval scripts.
[44:10] Toni: We'll wait for the SOC2/HIPAA doc and contract addendum.
[44:18] Marco: Looking forward to the POC.

[46:30] Samir: Thanks all — we'll end here.
